earlier_scan.source_named: Rivierre, J.-C. & S. Ehrhart 2006, Le bwatoo et les dialectes de la region de Kone (Nouvelle-Caledonie) (251pp grammar sketch, Glottolog MED 55944); not online

sources.note: Lists only Pangloss texts, Glottolog, Ethnologue and a trilingual children's book (Hurly 2011); no language description other than via Glottolog (= Rivierre & Ehrhart 2006).

sources.citation: Rohleder, Jean. 2024. A grammar of Vamale (Language Science Press). Text on file:
sources.note: Sec. 5.6 Stress (pp. 80-82) describes VAMALE (vama1243), a sister Voh-Koné dialect: penultimate in disyllables, initial in simple trisyllables, hierarchy long syllable > fortis onset > closed syllable > penult; reports Campbell 1987:59 for Hmwaveke (fundamentally penultimate) and Bril 2002 for Nêlêmwa (root-initial). Cites Rivierre & Ehrhart 2006 pp. 25-27 only for Bwatoo segmental facts (nasal vowels, fortis/aspirated consonants); says nothing about Bwatoo stress.

sources.citation: Bensa, Alban [with Jean-Claude Rivierre]. 2022. Du mot-à-mot au « faste mental ». Enquêtes linguistiques et ethnolinguistiques en Nouvelle-Calédonie. Jean-Claude Rivierre (1938-2018). In: Uane nore nodei lanengoce / Penser les langues, pp. 22-46. Nouméa: Presses universitaires de la Nouvelle-Calédonie (coll. LA-NI). HAL hal-05582019.
sources.note: Image-only PDF, scanned (tesseract fra). Retrospective of Rivierre's career; mentions his Bwatoo work with R. Diéla and lists the 2006 book. Only prosodic remark is general: tonogenesis becomes understandable when the Kanak tone languages are compared with neighbours 'qui marquent des accents en particulier sur la première syllabe (Moyse-Faurie, 2018)'. No statement about Bwatoo stress.

sources.citation: LACITO-CNRS language page 'bwatoo / Bwatoo [Voh-Kone dialect]' (lacito.vjf.cnrs.fr/ALC/Languages/Bwatoo_popup.htm, Wayback 2020-12-05) and LACITO publication notice for Rivierre & Ehrhart 2006 (vient-de-paraitre/rivierre_bwatoo.htm) and Rivierre member page.
sources.note: Bibliographic only; the sole publication on Bwatoo listed is Rivierre & Ehrhart 2006; blurb has no phonology.
